title: Short Proofs for the Minimum Number of Determined Circles
title_ko: 결정된 원의 최소 개수에 대한 짧은 증명
abstract: We present short proofs for the main parts of the recently completed solution of Erdős Problem 506, which asks for the minimum number of distinct circles determined by a finite planar point set that is neither collinear nor concyclic. An inversion argument and a seven-point line lemma show that eight points determine at least $17$ circles, and an explicit configuration attains this bound. A single argument combining Melchior's inequality with Langer's incidence bound establishes the sharp formula for every $n\ge15$. The proofs give concise alternatives to longer arguments in the recent literature; the remaining finite cases are cited separately.

conventions: Use `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` for the real plane. Points are elements of this type.
Represent finite point sets as `Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))`.
Use `SimpleGraph` or explicit `Finset` of lines/circles for incidence structures if needed, but prefer direct set-theoretic definitions for clarity in this combinatorial geometry context.
Define 'admissible' point sets explicitly: non-collinear and non-concyclic.
Use `Nat` for cardinalities and indices. Use `ℝ` for coordinates and distances.
Inversion is a map `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`; define it explicitly with center and radius (usually unit radius).
Lines and circles are represented by their defining equations or geometric objects in Mathlib (`AffineSubspace` for lines, `Metric.sphere` or custom `Circle` structure for circles).
Use `Finset.card` for counting points, lines, and circles.
Asymptotic statements are not used; all bounds are exact integer inequalities.
conventions_ko: 실수 평면은 `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`로 표현한다. 점은 이 타입의 원소이다.
직선과 원의 교차 구조가 필요하면 `SimpleGraph`나 명시적인 `Finset`을 사용하되, 조합기하학적 맥락에서는 명확성을 위해 집합론적 정의를 우선한다.
'허용된(admissible)' 점 집합을 명시적으로 정의한다: 공선점이 아니며 공원점도 아니다.
기수 및 인덱스는 `Nat`을, 좌표 및 거리는 `ℝ`을 사용한다.
반전(inversion)은 `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` 사상이다. 중심과 반지름(보통 단위 반지름)을 사용하여 명시적으로 정의한다.
직선과 원은 정의 방정식이나 Mathlib의 기하학적 객체(직선은 `AffineSubspace`, 원은 `Metric.sphere` 또는 사용자 정의 `Circle` 구조체)로 표현한다.
점, 직선, 원의 개수를 셀 때 `Finset.card`를 사용한다.
점근적 진술은 사용하지 않으며, 모든 상한은 정확한 정수 부등식이다.
definitions:
import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace Arxiv261018918

/-- A finite set of points $P$ is admissible if it is neither collinear nor concyclic. -/
def IsAdmissible (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : Prop :=
  ¬Collinear ℝ (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) ∧
  ¬∃ (center : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (radius : ℝ),
    ∀ p ∈ P, dist p center = radius

/-- The number of distinct circles determined by a set of points $P$. A circle is determined by any non-collinear triple of points in $P$. Distinct circles are counted once even if they contain more than three points from $P$. -/
noncomputable def numCircles (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℕ :=
  Set.ncard { c : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) | 
    (∃ a b d, a ∈ P ∧ b ∈ P ∧ d ∈ P ∧ a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ d ∧ a ≠ d ∧ 
      ¬Collinear ℝ {a, b, d} ∧ a ∈ c ∧ b ∈ c ∧ d ∈ c) ∧
    (∃ center : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), ∃ radius : ℝ, c = Metric.sphere center radius) }

/-- The minimum number of distinct circles determined by an admissible set of $n$ points. -/
noncomputable def minCircles (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf { k : ℕ | ∃ P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), P.card = n ∧ IsAdmissible P ∧ numCircles P = k }

/-- The upper bound function $g(n) = 1 + \binom{n-1}{2} - \lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor$. -/
def standardBound (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  1 + Nat.choose (n - 1) 2 - (n - 1) / 2

/-- The inversion map with respect to a point $p$ (center) and unit radius. Maps a point $x \neq p$ to $x'$ such that $p, x, x'$ are collinear, $p$ is between $x$ and $x'$ (or $x=x'$), and $\text{dist } p x \cdot \text{dist } p x' = 1$. -/
noncomputable def invert (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) :=
  if x = p then p else
    let v := x - p
    let d := ‖v‖
    p + (1 / d^2) • v

end Arxiv261018918

items.tex:
The minimum number of circles satisfies
\[
 f(8)=17,\qquad f(n)=g(n)\quad\text{for every }n\ge15.
\]
items.title_en: Minimum number of circles for n=8 and n>=15
items.title_ko: n=8 및 n>=15일 때 원의 최소 개수
items.statement_en: The minimum number of distinct circles determined by an admissible set of $n$ points, denoted $f(n)$, satisfies $f(8) = 17$. Furthermore, for every integer $n \ge 15$, $f(n)$ equals the standard upper bound $g(n) = 1 + \binom{n-1}{2} - \lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor$.
items.statement_ko: n개의 점으로 이루어진 허용 가능한 집합이 결정하는 서로 다른 원의 최소 개수 $f(n)$에 대하여, $f(8) = 17$이 성립한다. 또한, 모든 정수 $n \ge 15$에 대하여 $f(n)$은 표준 상한 $g(n) = 1 + \binom{n-1}{2} - \lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor$과 같다.
items.lean: (n : ℕ) (hn : 15 ≤ n) : minCircles 8 = 17 ∧ minCircles n = standardBound n
items.note: The theorem combines two distinct claims: the exact value for n=8 and the equality with the standard bound for n>=15. The Lean statement uses a conjunction to capture both parts under the hypothesis n >= 15, although the first part (n=8) is independent of n. Alternatively, this could be split into two theorems, but the prompt asks for 'ONE result' corresponding to the displayed equation block. The definition of `standardBound` uses integer division `/` which corresponds to floor division for natural numbers in Lean.

items.name: Initial parallel investigations
items.tex:
\Cref{thm:main} was obtained in the summer of 2026 by (at least) five investigations 
within a short period: those of Rafa\l{} Wrona, Liyan Wang, Stijn Cambie,
Denis Paliy, and the forum (on~\cite{Forum506}) user \texttt{mzn}. These investigations were independent, assuming that their AI use would not influence each other (which is unclear). This paper summarises the main insights from those.\\
The block-counting/inversion approach for eight points and the uniform
incidence approach for $n\ge15$ also appear in~\cite{Wrona}.
The seven-point Lemma~\ref{lem:seven} and the pointed
Lemma~\ref{lem:pointed} yield short versions of these arguments.
The carrier estimate, inversion count, and Melchior argument after
adjoining the inversion centre have counterparts in
\cite[Lemmas~2.1, 2.2 and 6.1]{Wang}; the proof in~\cite{Wang} treats
$n=15$ and $n=16$ separately. Paliy's parallel work~\cite{PaliyCorrected}
developed an exact computational and SAT-based approach to the finite
cases, e.g. $n=12,13$, with reproducible verification files.

Seven real planar points with no four collinear determine at most six
three-point lines. If there are six, every point outside the set lies
on at most one ordinary line and at most one three-point line.
items.statement_en: Let $P$ be a set of 7 points in the real plane such that no four points are collinear. Then $P$ determines at most 6 three-point lines. If $P$ determines exactly 6 three-point lines, then for any point $q \notin P$, $q$ lies on at most one ordinary line (a line containing exactly 2 points of $P$) and at most one three-point line (a line containing exactly 3 points of $P$).
items.statement_ko: 실수 평면에서 네 점이 일직선 위에 있지 않은 7개의 점으로 이루어진 집합 $P$가 있다고 하자. 그러면 $P$는 최대 6개의 세 점 직선을 결정한다. 만약 $P$가 정확히 6개의 세 점 직선을 결정한다면, $P$에 속하지 않는 임의의 점 $q$에 대해, $q$는 최대 하나의 보통 직선($P$의 점 정확히 2개를 포함하는 직선)과 최대 하나의 세 점 직선($P$의 점 정확히 3개를 포함하는 직선) 위에 놓인다.

items.title_en: Inequality for lines not passing through an external point
items.title_ko: 외부 점을 지나지 않는 직선들에 대한 부등식
items.statement_en:
Let $Q$ be a non-collinear set of $m$ points in the real plane, and let $o$ be a point not in $Q$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the set of lines spanned by pairs of distinct points in $Q$. For each line $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$, let $j_\ell = |\ell \cap Q|$. Then the following inequality holds:
\[
 \sum_{\substack{\ell\in\mathcal{L}\\o\notin\ell}}\frac{1}{j_\ell+1}
 \ge \frac{1}{12}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}}j_\ell-\frac{m}{9}+\frac{1}{2}.
\]
items.statement_ko:
$Q$를 실수 평면 위의 비공선(non-collinear)인 $m$개의 점의 집합이라 하고, $o$를 $Q$에 속하지 않는 점이라 하자. $\mathcal{L}$을 $Q$의 서로 다른 두 점에 의해 생성되는 직선들의 집합이라 하자. 각 직선 $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$에 대해 $j_\ell = |\ell \cap Q|$라 할 때, 다음 부등식이 성립한다:
\[
 \sum_{\substack{\ell\in\mathcal{L}\\o\notin\ell}}\frac{1}{j_\ell+1}
 \ge \frac{1}{12}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}}j_\ell-\frac{m}{9}+\frac{1}{2}.
\]
